method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of the three closure proofs, with exact formula, macro, label and reference parity. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Closure of computably enumerable sets under binary union and intersection, using total enumerators and partial computable domains.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If A and B are c.e., so are their intersection and union. The equivalence theorem permits several characterizations. An empty input set makes the intersection empty and the union the other input set; thereafter the first two arguments take total computable enumerators of both nonempty sets.
samples.checks: Both operations, theorem hypothesis, equivalence reference and empty-set qualification are preserved. OLCMP-019 documents the omitted source scope case.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For nonempty A and B enumerated by f and g, the partial search h finds x in either enumeration and has domain A union B. The search j uses the two coordinates of y to find x in both enumerations and has domain A intersection B. These searches give one-sided semidecision procedures.
samples.checks: The disjunction versus conjunction, pair-coordinate indices, domain statements and parallel search meaning match the frozen formulas.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Alternating even and odd inputs to f and g yields a total enumerator k of the union. If the intersection is empty it is c.e.; otherwise choose c in it. The total l examines paired enumerated values and returns a match when they agree, falling back to c otherwise, so its range is the intersection.
samples.checks: Parity branches, half-indices, nonempty witness c, equality test and fallback value remain exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If A and B are the domains of partial functions m and n, the domain of m(x)+n(x) is their intersection because both must halt. For the union, indices d and e let p search for a T witness of halting by either computation in parallel. Its domain is the union.
samples.checks: The intersection uses both halting conditions, while union uses T(d,x,y) or T(e,x,y). The exact indexed formulas and final halting explanation are retained.

source_observations: T017 and T018 distinguish union and intersection; T327 supplies effective-enumeration terminology and T328 supplies one-sided semidecision terminology under OpenLogic definitions.
OLCMP-019 adds the empty-input-set case in prose before the first two enumerator proofs. No protected formula changes were required.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The exact Marathi compound for computably enumerable remains expert-reviewable.
